findings.title: Cloud data platforms dominate location-based CO2
findings.explanation: The two data-platform estates together account for just over half of baseline CO2, while also taking more than a quarter of recurring spend. They are the main decarbonisation lever.

findings.title: SaaS and AI subscriptions are a major cost block
findings.explanation: Licence-heavy services are a large share of spend, so seat hygiene matters for the cost target even if energy impact is small.

findings.title: Development data platform runs 24/7 despite very low active time
findings.explanation: The dev cluster runs all day every day, but is idle 91.32% of running hours and shows only 8.7% average CPU utilisation. This is the single biggest avoidable CO2 source.

findings.title: Non-production compute is left on continuously
findings.explanation: The GPU server runs 100% of hours with about 9% average GPU utilisation, while the test estate averages only 10.89% CPU and still includes near-dead servers with hundreds of days since login.

findings.title: There is large licence waste from inactive seats
findings.explanation: Several products carry large inactive-seat spend. The biggest single pools are Microsoft Copilot, CRM, video conferencing, E-signature and ChatGPT Team.

findings.title: Low-risk AI tasks still use expensive large models by default
findings.explanation: The office assistant already has small-model paths for several tasks, but most spending remains on large models. Marketing classification is also entirely on a large model although the task is structurally simpler than free-form generation.

measures.title: Auto-pause and region-move the development data platform
measures.description: Schedule the dev cluster to start only for working windows and quarter-day processing, with on-demand wake-up for exceptions. After the schedule is in place, move the remaining workload from DE to CH to cut grid CO2 on the residual load.

effects.reasoning: The cluster runs 24 h/day but averages only 2.846 active hours on weekdays and 0.2139 on weekends, with 91.32% idle time. Keeping full availability on quarter days 1-3 Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct and leaving buffer for warm-up/on-demand use still supports cutting roughly 85% of billed node-hours. The remaining 15% can be moved from DE to CH for lower location-based CO2.

measures.effort_reasoning: Needs schedule design, IaC/job changes, start-stop automation, testing of cold-start times, and a controlled regional move for a low-criticality dev platform.
measures.status_reason: Safe technically, but the region move and tighter availability window need explicit IT approval and developer acceptance.
measures.risks: Unexpected ad-hoc developer work outside the schedule may need an override; regional move may require endpoint or latency checks.
measures.assumptions: Billing falls roughly linearly with node-hours removed; C-03 quarter-day continuous availability is preserved.

measures.title: Auto-stop the GPU ML server outside quarterly training and booked runs
measures.description: Keep the GPU environment off by default, start it for quarterly training days and approved ad-hoc runs only, and shut it down automatically after inactivity.

effects.reasoning: The GPU server runs 100% of hours, but average GPU utilisation is only 9.19% and median weekly utilisation 6.45%. Since quarterly training days account for only a small part of annual spend, keeping the server on for those protected days plus booked ad-hoc sessions still leaves a realistic 82% removable share.

measures.effort_reasoning: Single-server automation with inactivity shutdown, runbook update and validation around quarterly training windows.
measures.status_reason: Low-criticality dev workload with a clear protected quarterly window; the measure keeps those days fully available.
measures.risks: Users may forget to pre-book ad-hoc runs; mitigated with self-service start and inactivity timeout.
measures.assumptions: Quarterly training remains the main planned usage pattern and ad-hoc work can tolerate startup delay.

measures.effort_reasoning: Cross-product seat audit, department confirmations, notice handling, contract-change requests and billing verification across many vendors.
measures.status_reason: Seat removals need department sign-off to avoid cancelling genuinely reserved seats for near-term hires or shared-team use.

measures.title: Route low-risk office-assistant tasks to small models by default
measures.description: For summarisation, translation, drafting and general manual questions, make the small model the default and keep the large model as fallback for difficult prompts.

effects.reasoning: Move about 80% of summarise traffic to the small model. With small/large price ratio 0.30, cost saving is 0.8 × 0.70 = 0.56; energy saving is 0.8 × 0.75 = 0.60.
Move about 80% of translation traffic to the small model. With small/large price ratio 0.30, cost saving is 0.8 × 0.70 = 0.56; energy saving is 0.8 × 0.75 = 0.60.
Move about 60% of drafting traffic to the small model and leave the rest on large for harder prompts. Cost saving is 0.6 × 0.70 = 0.42; energy saving is 0.6 × 0.75 = 0.45.
Move about 50% of generic manual-question traffic to the small model while keeping large as fallback. Cost saving is 0.5 × 0.70 = 0.35; energy saving is 0.5 × 0.75 = 0.375.

measures.effort_reasoning: Prompt-routing change, fallback logic, quick UAT with key users and communication of the new default.
measures.status_reason: Quality sign-off is needed because users may notice different answer quality on some prompts.
measures.risks: A few users may route difficult prompts to the large model more often than expected; savings depend on keeping the fallback exception-based.
measures.assumptions: These tasks remain human-reviewed or low-risk enough for a small-model default.

measures.title: Switch marketing classification mostly to a small model
measures.description: Use a small model as the default for marketing text classification, with escalation to the large model only for uncertain cases.

effects.reasoning: Classification is narrower than free-form generation, so moving about 85% of requests to a small model is realistic. Cost saving is 0.85 × 0.70 = 0.595; energy saving is 0.85 × 0.75 = 0.6375.

measures.effort_reasoning: Single routing rule change plus sample-based quality check with marketing.
measures.status_reason: Marketing should validate classification quality before making small-model routing the default.
measures.risks: Misclassification may increase if prompts or labels are poorly defined; fallback to the large model must remain available.
measures.assumptions: The one-off bug spike in March is ignored; the change is sized from normal recurring classification demand.

measures.title: Delete third backup copies to save storage
measures.description: Remove the third copy from sources backed up by all three tools and shorten backup holdings.

effects.reasoning: The fact pattern suggests up to 14.82% of backup volume sits in third copies, so deleting those copies would remove the same share of storage cost and energy.

measures.effort_reasoning: Would be simple technically, but is not permissible.
measures.status_reason: Do not recommend: backup deletion is explicitly blocked by legal-retention constraints.
measures.risks: Legal and audit breach; possible loss of required recoverability.
measures.assumptions: None; shown only as an excluded edge case.

measures.title: Shut down the DR failover server
measures.description: Turn off the failover environment because it is nearly idle.

effects.reasoning: Measured use is near zero, so full shutdown would save the whole server if it were allowed.

measures.effort_reasoning: Technically easy, but forbidden by policy.
measures.status_reason: Do not recommend: the DR server must remain running as emergency fallback.
measures.assumptions: None; shown only as an excluded edge case.

package.reasoning: This package still fits the implementation budget and now clears the CO2 and cost targets by prioritising always-on non-production compute first, then adding licence hygiene and safe AI model routing. Human decisions are still needed for the dp-dev region move and schedule, test-environment operating windows, seat reductions by department, and AI quality sign-off.

edge_cases.explanation: Backup deletion looks tempting because third copies exist, but it directly conflicts with the legal-retention blocks on st-backup and must stay out of the package.
The DR failover server is almost idle, but policy explicitly requires it to stay running, so it is excluded despite apparent savings.
